gate.durability: Identity rows are reserved 64 at a time in one FULL transaction. Each row is durable before attaching its xattr, and the inode remains synced before manifest publication. The schema and publication/retirement ordering are unchanged.
gate.tests: Two concurrent connections allocate distinct identities across batch boundaries; offline GC discards unused reservations without recycling IDs and the same Live instance can allocate afterward. Injected partial-batch failure rolls back all rows without attaching an xattr. Process death before commit, after reservation, and after inode sync preserves native bytes and allows GC/reseal. Existing filesystem/Cargo/recovery suites pass.

limitations: Two reversed-order rounds on a shared node, not a statistical significance claim.
Warm OS caches; debug incremental only.
CPU idle observation does not prove background sealing drained.
Cumulative phase times overlap; they are not added Cargo latency.
Two workers in both SL7 cases; fixed source/profile/output paths; the candidate batches durable identity reservations.
